questions.prompt: Which animal is the largest on Earth?
questions.note: A blue whale can be about 30 metres long.

questions.prompt: Bats are mammals.
questions.note: Bats are the only mammals that can truly fly.

questions.prompt: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.note: Two pump blood through the gills and one pumps it around the body.

questions.prompt: What is the name for a baby kangaroo?
questions.note: A joey stays in its mother's pouch for months.

questions.prompt: Which is the fastest land animal over a short distance?
questions.note: A cheetah can sprint faster than cars drive in towns.

questions.prompt: Sharks are mammals.
questions.note: Sharks are fish. They breathe with gills.

questions.prompt: What is a group of lions called?
questions.note: Lions are the only big cats that live in social groups.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the process plants use to make food from sunlight?
questions.note: Plants take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen while doing it.

questions.prompt: How many bones does an adult human body usually have?
questions.note: Babies are born with more, and some join together as they grow.

questions.prompt: Which insect makes honey?
questions.note: Honey bees visit flowers to collect nectar.

questions.prompt: How many planets are in our Solar System?
questions.note: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

questions.prompt: Which star is closest to Earth?
questions.note: The Sun is about 150 million kilometres away.

questions.prompt: Sound travels faster than light.
questions.note: Light is far faster, which is why you see lightning before you hear thunder.

questions.prompt: Which gas do humans need to breathe in to stay alive?
questions.note: Plants make a lot of the oxygen we breathe.

questions.prompt: At what temperature in degrees Celsius does water boil at sea level?
questions.note: On a high mountain it boils at a lower temperature.

questions.prompt: Which planet is famous for its bright rings?
questions.note: Saturn's rings are made of ice and rock.

questions.prompt: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.note: This happened in July 1969.

questions.prompt: What force pulls objects towards the Earth?
questions.note: Gravity keeps the Moon going around the Earth too.

questions.prompt: What is the hardest natural substance?
questions.note: Diamonds are made of carbon.

questions.prompt: Which of these metals is attracted to a magnet?
questions.note: Steel is mostly iron, so magnets stick to it.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of France?
questions.note: The Eiffel Tower is in Paris.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest ocean?
questions.note: It covers about a third of the Earth's surface.

questions.prompt: How many continents are there, using the most common way of counting?
questions.note: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia/Oceania, Europe, North America and South America.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.note: The Sahara covers about nine million square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which mountain is the highest above sea level?
questions.note: It lies on the border of Nepal and Tibet.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Australia?
questions.note: Many people guess Sydney, but Canberra was built to be the capital.

questions.prompt: Which country is shaped a little like a boot?
questions.note: Sicily looks like a football being kicked by the boot.

questions.prompt: On which continent is Egypt?
questions.note: Egypt's Sinai Peninsula is in Asia, but most of the country is in Africa.

questions.prompt: Which country is the Great Wall famous for being in?
questions.note: Parts of the wall were built over many centuries.

questions.prompt: Antarctica is the coldest continent.
questions.note: Temperatures there have dropped below minus 80 degrees Celsius.

questions.prompt: Who wrote the Harry Potter books?
questions.note: The first book came out in 1997.

questions.prompt: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.note: It hangs in the Louvre museum in Paris.

questions.prompt: Who were the great pyramids of Egypt built for?
questions.note: Pharaohs were the rulers of ancient Egypt.

questions.prompt: In which year did the Wright brothers make the first powered aeroplane flight?
questions.note: The first flight lasted about 12 seconds.

questions.prompt: Which huge ship sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg?
questions.note: It was on its first voyage.

questions.prompt: Who wrote Charlie and the Chocolate Factory?
questions.note: Roald Dahl also wrote Matilda and The BFG.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the lion in The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe?
questions.note: C. S. Lewis wrote the Narnia books.

questions.prompt: Which wall did the Romans build across northern England?
questions.note: Parts of it still stand after nearly 1,900 years.

questions.prompt: Viking warriors wore helmets with horns in battle.
questions.note: There is no good evidence for it. The idea became popular through 19th-century art.

questions.prompt: Which language is mostly spoken in Brazil?
questions.note: Brazil was ruled by Portugal for over 300 years.

questions.prompt: How many players from one team are on the pitch in a football (soccer) match?
questions.note: That includes the goalkeeper.

questions.prompt: How many rings are in the Olympic symbol?
questions.note: They stand for five regions of the world joined together.

questions.prompt: Which sport is played at Wimbledon?
questions.note: Wimbledon is played on grass courts.

questions.prompt: What is 7 multiplied by 8?
questions.note: A handy trick is 5, 6, 7, 8: 56 equals 7 times 8.

questions.prompt: How many sides does an octagon have?
questions.note: Stop signs are often octagons.

questions.prompt: Which number is shown by the Roman numeral X?
questions.note: V is 5, L is 50 and C is 100.

questions.prompt: What is bread mainly made from?
questions.note: Flour is usually ground from wheat.

questions.prompt: Which musical instrument has black and white keys?
questions.note: Its full name is pianoforte, which means soft-loud.

questions.prompt: What do the letters www stand for in a web address?
questions.note: Tim Berners-Lee invented the web.

questions.prompt: How many strings does a standard violin have?
questions.note: They are tuned G, D, A and E.
